scope: Fifteenth expansion batch: 12 controlled exercises, three each for a stated hodo degree, a below-standard hodo comparison, V-ba V-ru hodo correlated change, and V-tai dake desired extent. This is not unrestricted discrimination between hodo, kurai and dake, or exhaustive coverage of their extent patterns.

sources.section: Actual HTML heading ほど【程】［副助・連語］, particle senses 2 (degree illustrated by a situation), 3 (a comparison standard with negation), and 4 (correlated change). Simplified extraction showed a different dictionary; the modern Daijisen entry was inspected directly.

A wa B hodo ... nai comparisons, including adjective negatives with optional emphatic wa, and clause-based degree descriptions. The negative requirement belongs to the not-as comparison, not every hodo construction.

Actual HTML Structure/About: a verb's ba form followed by its dictionary form and hodo; Related distinguishes correlated change from simple intensification. The conditional portion can be omitted in other formulations; this batch deliberately requests the full pattern.

Actual HTML of Using hodo to express the extent of something: a negative reference-degree sentence, a clause-based high degree, and correlated-change examples including becoming more lost with more walking. Broader claims about conditional alternatives or adjective restrictions are not adopted.

Particle sense 1 for amount/extent and attachment to attributive predicates; sense 3a also records ba ... dake correlated change. Thus hodo and dake are not globally separated by the two functions practiced in this batch.

Tai attaches to the verb's masu stem to express a desired action and inflects like an i-adjective. Combined with dake's extent use, it supplies the desired-amount pattern. Blanket claims about first-person restriction or ga always expressing stronger desire than wo are not adopted.

The particle entry 丈 read dake, sense 2 for extent/as much as. Supports the accepted particle spelling, not a claim that it is common. This exact entry was inspected during the preceding particle batch on the same retrieval date; not the separate take noun or mountain homographs.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original and need independent linguistic review. Source-backed meanings and attachment rules do not automatically attest the invented sentences.

Six adjective blanks request standard plain nonpast affirmative/negative forms without added particles, with desu printed. The same three adjectives occur on both sides. Negation before hodo in the heavy-box and expensive-watch items must not be confused with a negative main adjective.

Below-standard items specify relative weight, price or felt temperature. Not as heavy/expensive/cold does not assert complete absence of the property. Emphatic wa, other tenses and longer reformulations are outside the visible form restriction, not globally wrong.

The other six blanks request a complete named pattern: ba-form + dictionary form + hodo, or tai-form + dake. The same three verbs occur on both sides. All kana/kanji combinations for repeated verbs and particle spellings are included; no already printed verb or ending belongs inside the blank.
The correlated-change pattern can have an unwelcome result, as in growing confusion. No universal improvement or mathematical linearity is claimed.

The full article inventory was screened. Kurai can overlap with clause-based degree, dake can appear in correlated-change patterns, and shorter V-ru hodo or alternative desire/extent formulations can be natural. The printed material and named full-pattern restriction deliberately avoid false unrestricted rejection.

The desired-extent questions cover V-tai dake, not all possible-extent uses such as dekiru dake or potential-verb + dake. Other degree/minimum kurai and additional formal-noun uses still need dedicated practice.
All prior 197 exercise records remain unchanged against the committed preservationBaseline. Stable exercise IDs, not spellings or presentation modes, define the SRS identities.
